data.why: The app bundles its own curated example tables per plot type (examples/by_plot_type/*/data.csv) and a built-in 'Bundled sample' picker in the sidebar, so real-looking data is already available without synthesizing any.

goals: Load a dose-response CSV (viability vs. concentration per drug) and produce a publication-style dose-response curve
Compare a continuous measurement across three groups (Healthy/Disease/Treated) with a box or violin plot and run the matching statistical test (e.g. one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis)
Map columns from an uploaded table to the chosen plot type and confirm the suggested roles rather than accept silent guesses
Adjust the manuscript Publication style (typography, palette, axes, legend) and confirm it applies correctly to the chosen plot
Assemble two or more generated plots into a multi-panel Figure Builder composite with panel labels
Export the figure (SVG/PNG/PDF) together with its machine-readable PlotSpec/StatsSpec JSON sidecar

review.summary: The tree follows the README's single-plot workflow faithfully: load, recommend, map, style, test, export with specs. Every screen I opened supports its node, and the statistics and export branches are especially well documented. The goal leaves out multi-panel figures, which is half of what the tool says it is for. Presets, reopening saved specs, table preparation and annotations are also missing, and most style, statistics and export tasks were never replayed, so it needs those fixes before filing.
